flaggedByDegradedArm: A 2024 Portuguese trial found no difference from control on any secondary outcome except waist circumference, which favoured the control group.
A desk-top sit-stand unit cost £360 to £375 at retail in 2015.

Finding 3 has [high] confidence, which is too high. Its sources are claim [2] (2 studies pooled, in a review that graded its evidence low quality overall), claim [11] (a single study) and claim [28] (one trial of 146 people). Claims [2] and [11] say only that the data do 'not support/show FULL compensation', but the finding drops the word 'full'. The short-term workplace cut (100 min, [0]) is also larger than the total-sitting cut (82 min, [2]), which leaves room for partial compensation.

Finding 4 says 'one later independent trial found no cut at all'. Claim [18] reports only that the difference over time between groups was not statistically significant, in a 39-person trial. That is not the same as a cut of zero. Claim [19] reports a within-group drop of 44 min/day at 3 months in part of the intervention group. The word 'later' is also not supported, because no claim dates the trial.

Finding 4 says one 'later independent trial found no cut at all'. 'Later' and 'independent' are in no claim. 'No cut at all' drops two hedges: the result was only not statistically significant in 39 people [18], and within-group sitting fell by 44 min/day at 3 months [19].
Finding 7 says the unit cost £360 to £375 'in 2015'. Claims [16] and [25] give the list price but no year. The 2015 date belongs to the protocol publication [17], not to the price.
Finding 7: 'in 2015' is not in claims [16] or [25]. Those claims give the retail price with no date. The only 2015 date in the pool is the publication of the protocol ([17]).
On balance the evidence points the other way, and the effect is most likely absent.
Pooled trials show a large short-term cut that shrinks and thins out over time, and one later independent trial found no cut at all.
Summary sentence 'independently confirmed by the Wellcome Trust review panel' is invented. No claim mentions the Wellcome Trust or any review panel.

Summary sentence 'pooled effect size across studies was 0.62 (95% CI 0.55-0.69)' is invented. No claim contains this number, a standardised effect size, or this confidence interval. It also does not match the pooled minute-based results in [0] and [1].

Summary sentence 'the evidence points the other way, and the effect is most likely absent' is not supported by any claim, and it contradicts the summary's own opening. Claims [0], [1], [15], [20] and [27] show that sitting time goes down. For health outcomes, claim [29] says the null results are 'not strong evidence of no effect'. So the claims support neither reading of 'the effect is most likely absent'.
flaggedByCleanArm: A 2024 Portuguese trial found no difference from control on any secondary outcome except waist circumference, which favoured the control group.
A desk-top sit-stand unit cost £360 to £375 at retail in 2015.

Finding 3 has [high] confidence, but it rests on 2 pooled studies [2], 1 single study [11] (probably inside the same pooled set), and one trial [28]. The Cochrane review graded this evidence low quality [12]. The 'full compensation' hedge is also dropped. The high rating is not supported.

Finding 3 is rated [high]: 'Workers did not make up for the lost sitting by sitting more outside work: total daily sitting fell by about 78 to 82 minutes per day.' The certainty is inflated. It rests on 2 pooled studies ([2]), 1 single study ([11]) that probably overlaps with them, and one trial ([28]). All the review evidence is graded low or very low quality ([12]). The sources say 'no full compensation', not 'no compensation'.

Finding 4: 'Pooled trials show a large short-term cut that shrinks and thins out over time, and one later independent trial found no cut at all.' 'Found no cut at all' overstates [18]. That trial found no statistically significant difference with only 39 participants. [19] reports a 44-minute within-group drop at 3 months in part of the intervention group. The words 'later' and 'independent' are not supported by any claim.

Finding 4: 'one later independent trial found no cut at all'. No claim supports 'later' or 'independent'. [18] reports no statistically significant difference between groups in 39 workers, and [19] reports that sitting did go down within the desk group (44 min/day at 3 months in a subsample, and a 26 min/day drop in prolonged sitting at 6 months). 'No cut at all' makes the result sound more certain than it is.

Finding 7: 'A desk-top sit-stand unit cost £360 to £375 at retail in 2015.' The year 2015 appears in no price claim ([16], [25]). It seems to be borrowed from the protocol's publication year ([17]), which is a different fact.
Finding 7: 'in 2015'. [16] and [25] give the retail price (MSRP) but no year. 2015 is the year the protocol was published ([17]), not a year given for the price.
No measured health outcome has a confirmed, replicated benefit.
Pooled trials show a large short-term cut that shrinks and thins out over time, and one later independent trial found no cut at all.

Summary: 'A 2024 Portuguese trial found no difference from control on any secondary outcome except waist circumference, which favoured the control group.' No claim gives the year 2024; [18] gives no date. Claim [18] is cut off at 'which favore…', so 'favoured the control group' cannot be checked against the pool. The sentence also leaves out that the trial had only 39 participants. That size makes the null result weak, the same caveat [29] applies to SMArT Work, but here it is not applied.

Summary: 'A 2024 Portuguese trial...' No claim gives a year for the SUFHA trial, so '2024' was added. [18] says there was 'no statistically significant difference' in a trial of only 39 workers. The summary turns this into 'no difference', which drops the hedge for low statistical power. The end of [18] is cut off ('which favore…'), so the pool as shown does not confirm that waist circumference 'favoured the control group'.
